title: Sweet tooth hazards
titleChinese: 爱吃甜食给健康带来的隐患
paragraphs: Sweet or savoury? Which flavour do you prefer? If like me you have a sweet tooth, you probably can’t resist eating cake, biscuits or chocolate and you‘ll add a few spoonfuls of sugar to your tea or coffee — delicious! But this taste is easily able to ignore warnings that too much of the white stuff is bad for our health.

Consuming sugar is an addiction - the more we eat, the more we want. Today’s processed food, like ready meals, is laced with the stuff and many fizzy drinks contain seven teaspoons of sugar in just one can. In the UK, statistics show that sugar consumption is at its highest level in history and the government is trying to get the food industry to cut the amount of sugar in popular products like chocolate bars by 20% by 2020.

Of course, sugary food tastes nice, it can help lift our mood, and the glucose in it can give us an energy boost. But there are dangers too: a high-sugar diet is linked to obesity, and being overweight can increase the risk of getting type 2 diabetes. With these warning signs, I have considered changing my diet by replacing sugary snacks with fruit and savoury biscuits — but that‘s boring, I need my sugar fix!

I’m not alone. BBC journalist Radhika Shanghai, has gone one step further. Encouraged by some celebrities and nutritionists promoting a ‘zero tolerance‘ approach to sugar, she gave it up altogether, thinking it would make her healthier. Initially she says, “My first fortnight involves mood swings worse than puberty. I have agonising headaches and feel permanently hungover.” These symptoms disappeared but she still found food shopping hard as she was stressing about buying the right things.

Her experiment wasn’t a success. She eventually sought advice from Susan Jebb, professor of diet and population health at Oxford University who said: “Lots of people enjoy sugar and gain pleasure from it, so one has to find a balance between enjoyment and eating the right amount.”

There are health benefits of cutting down sugar such as improving dental care and reducing weight gain, but there‘s no need to be obsessive about it. Eating some sugar as part of a balanced diet is fine and exercising will help burn it off. So rather than dealing with your sugar cravings by cutting it out of your diet altogether, why not work on your willpower and learn to say ’no‘ to a second serving of chocolate fudge cheesecake.

vocabulary.entry: resist [v.] /rɪˈzɪst/ 抵制；抗拒
vocabulary.example: She couldn‘t resist the temptation of the chocolate cake.
vocabulary.translation: 她无法抗拒巧克力蛋糕的诱惑。

vocabulary.entry: addiction [n.] /əˈdɪkʃən/ 成瘾；上瘾 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Sugar addiction is difficult to overcome.
vocabulary.translation: 糖瘾很难克服。

vocabulary.entry: processed [adj.] /ˈprəʊsest/ 加工过的
vocabulary.example: Processed foods often contain high levels of sugar and salt.
vocabulary.translation: 加工食品通常含有高糖和高盐。

vocabulary.entry: laced [adj.] /leɪst/ 掺有……的；加有……的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The drink was laced with alcohol.
vocabulary.translation: 这种饮料里掺了酒。

vocabulary.entry: glucose [n.] /ˈɡluːkəʊs/ 葡萄糖 (生物化学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Glucose is the main source of energy for the body.
vocabulary.translation: 葡萄糖是身体的主要能量来源。

vocabulary.entry: obesity [n.] /əʊˈbiːsəti/ 肥胖；肥胖症 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Obesity increases the risk of many diseases.
vocabulary.translation: 肥胖增加许多疾病的风险。

vocabulary.entry: fix [n.] /fɪks/ 一次用量；一剂 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I need my morning coffee fix to wake up.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要早上喝杯咖啡来提神。

vocabulary.entry: hungover [adj.] /ˈhʌŋəʊvə/ 宿醉的；有宿醉反应的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He felt hungover after drinking too much at the party.
vocabulary.translation: 他在派对上喝多了，感觉宿醉未醒。

vocabulary.entry: obsessive [adj.] /əbˈsesɪv/ 着迷的；过度的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He has an obsessive need for order and cleanliness.
vocabulary.translation: 他对秩序和清洁有着过度的执念。

vocabulary.entry: cravings [n. pl.] /ˈkreɪvɪŋz/ 渴望；热望 (单数: craving；书面语)
vocabulary.example: Pregnant women often have unusual food cravings.
vocabulary.translation: 孕妇常常有不同寻常的食物渴望。

vocabulary.entry: savoury [adj.] /ˈseɪvəri/ 咸味的；味道浓郁的
vocabulary.example: I prefer savoury snacks to sweet ones.
vocabulary.translation: 比起甜食，我更喜欢咸味小吃。

vocabulary.entry: fizzy [adj.] /ˈfɪzi/ 起泡的；嘶嘶作响的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Fizzy drinks are high in sugar and calories.
vocabulary.translation: 碳酸饮料含糖量和热量都很高。

vocabulary.entry: statistics [n. pl.] /stəˈtɪstɪks/ 统计数据；统计资料 (单数: statistic)
vocabulary.example: The statistics show a rise in obesity among children.
vocabulary.translation: 统计数据显示儿童肥胖率在上升。

vocabulary.entry: consumption [n.] /kənˈsʌmpʃən/ 消费；消耗 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The consumption of sugar has increased dramatically.
vocabulary.translation: 糖的消费量急剧增加。

vocabulary.entry: boost [n.] /buːst/ 提高；增长
vocabulary.example: A short walk can give you an energy boost.
vocabulary.translation: 短暂散步可以给你提供能量。

vocabulary.entry: diabetes [n.] /ˌdaɪəˈbiːtiːz/ 糖尿病 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Type 2 diabetes is linked to diet and lifestyle.
vocabulary.translation: 2型糖尿病与饮食和生活方式有关。

vocabulary.entry: fortnight [n.] /ˈfɔːtnaɪt/ 两星期；十四天 (英式英语)
vocabulary.example: She is going on holiday for a fortnight.
vocabulary.translation: 她要去度假两周。

vocabulary.entry: mood swings [n. pl.] /ˈmuːd swɪŋz/ 情绪波动 (心理学词汇；单数: mood swing)
vocabulary.example: Hormonal changes can cause mood swings.
vocabulary.translation: 荷尔蒙变化会导致情绪波动。

vocabulary.entry: agonising [adj.] /ˈæɡənaɪzɪŋ/ 使人痛苦的；折磨人的
vocabulary.example: He had an agonising pain in his back.
vocabulary.translation: 他的背部疼痛难忍。

vocabulary.entry: willpower [n.] /ˈwɪlpaʊə/ 意志力；毅力
vocabulary.example: It takes a lot of willpower to quit smoking.
vocabulary.translation: 戒烟需要很大的意志力。

sentences.chinese: 但是这种味道很容易让我们忽视这样的警告：过多食用这种白色的东西（糖）对我们的健康有害。

sentences.chinese: 如今的加工食品，比如即食食品，都掺有这种东西（糖），许多碳酸饮料——罐里就含有七茶匙的糖。

sentences.chinese: 在英国，统计数据显示糖的消费量达到了历史最高水平，政府正试图让食品行业到2020年将巧克力棒等受欢迎产品中的糖含量降低20%。

sentences.english: Of course, sugary food tastes nice, it can help lift our mood, and the glucose in it can give us an energy boost.
sentences.chinese: 当然，含糖食品味道不错，它能帮助改善我们的心情，而且其中的葡萄糖能给我们提供能量。

sentences.english: But there are dangers too: a high-sugar diet is linked to obesity, and being overweight can increase the risk of getting type 2 diabetes.
sentences.chinese: 但也有危险：高糖饮食与肥胖症有关，而且超重会增加患2型糖尿病的风险。

sentences.english: With these warning signs, I have considered changing my diet by replacing sugary snacks with fruit and savoury biscuits — but that‘s boring, I need my sugar fix!
sentences.chinese: 有了这些警告信号，我曾考虑改变我的饮食，用水果和咸味饼干来代替含糖零食——但那很无聊，我需要来点糖！

sentences.english: I’m not alone.
sentences.chinese: 我并不孤单。

sentences.english: BBC journalist Radhika Shanghai, has gone one step further.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司记者拉迪卡·尚哈尼更进一步。

sentences.english: Encouraged by some celebrities and nutritionists promoting a ‘zero tolerance‘ approach to sugar, she gave it up altogether, thinking it would make her healthier.
sentences.chinese: 在一些名人和营养学家提倡对糖采取“零容忍”态度的鼓励下，她完全戒掉了糖，认为这样会让她更健康。

sentences.english: Initially she says, “My first fortnight involves mood swings worse than puberty.
sentences.chinese: 起初她说：“我的头两周情绪波动比青春期还厉害。

sentences.english: I have agonising headaches and feel permanently hungover.”
sentences.chinese: 我头痛得厉害，而且一直感觉像是宿醉未醒。”

sentences.english: These symptoms disappeared but she still found food shopping hard as she was stressing about buying the right things.
sentences.chinese: 这些症状后来消失了，但她仍然觉得购买食品很难，因为她为买合适的东西而感到压力很大（还想买糖）。

sentences.english: Her experiment wasn’t a success.
sentences.chinese: 她的实验并不成功。

sentences.english: She eventually sought advice from Susan Jebb, professor of diet and population health at Oxford University who said: “Lots of people enjoy sugar and gain pleasure from it, so one has to find a balance between enjoyment and eating the right amount.”
sentences.chinese: 她最终向牛津大学饮食与人群健康教授苏珊·杰布寻求建议，苏珊·杰布说：“很多人喜欢糖，并从中获得乐趣，所以必须在享受和适量食用之间找到平衡。”

sentences.english: There are health benefits of cutting down sugar such as improving dental care and reducing weight gain, but there‘s no need to be obsessive about it.
sentences.chinese: 减少糖分摄入有很多健康益处，比如改善牙齿护理和减少体重增加，但也没必要对此过于执着。

sentences.english: Eating some sugar as part of a balanced diet is fine and exercising will help burn it off.
sentences.chinese: 在均衡饮食中吃一些糖是可以的，而且锻炼有助于消耗掉这些糖分。

sentences.english: So rather than dealing with your sugar cravings by cutting it out of your diet altogether, why not work on your willpower and learn to say ’no‘ to a second serving of chocolate fudge cheesecake.
sentences.chinese: 所以，与其完全从饮食中戒掉糖来应对对糖的渴望，为什么不锻炼自己的意志力，学会对第二份巧克力乳脂芝士蛋糕说“不”呢？
